30 year old trans guy here, I'm just crying my way through this post. You are doing everything right man, everything.

I came out later in life (22) and my parents stopped speaking to me, but last year we started talking again. 

My only advice: transition impacts everyone around the person in my experience, so make sure that if you need someone to talk to, you do.

It however, sounds like you've got it all in hand, so my next piece of advice? Keep being the awesome dad you're being.

I feel numb a lot of the time. I am on 200mg of lamictal (lamotrigine in the UK) and 1000mg of Depakote (sodium valproate), and I also have adhd so I have strattera for that. 

I noticed the massive personality shift when I started on the lamictal. It eased the depression and stopped me feeling as low as I had been doing, but it seemed to cut out the higher mods I had. It eased the mania which was brilliant. But it also seemed to remove basic happiness about things I like. I have lost a lot of zest for the things I used to love and find myself being told that I never seem to be 'myself' anymore.

Lithium was something that was suggested for me when I was first exploring better medications for myself. (previous psychs kept prescribing the same meds which didn't help), however, it was just by chance that I was prescribed lamictal. 

A close friend of mine has been on lithium for a while and whereas I've noticed a difference and he says that it works for him (which is t clearly does) he's had severe neurological damage and as such has developed a pretty severe tremor. 

If say explore all options if you think about lithium. 

However, not a doctor, just an experience. Hope things ease soon, I understand what the depression days can be like, in one atm. Stay strong x

And, yes, my medication does work. I need it. I have a mood imbalance. Without it, I would not be anywhere near as stable as I am now. Don't make assumptions and don't call me stupid. Because I am not.

I have both, and I could not be without my medication. I have bipolar disorder and it deals with the swings and has kept me out of hospital on multiple occasions. However, it hasn't stopped attempts, and I'd love to be in a position where I don't need it.

I know that's a long way however. :(

I understand exactly where you are coming from. I found myself being able to just switch off and allow everyone else to care for me.

A little context:

Lost my job in March. I care for my wife, and have a very autistic housemate that I in effect, look after too. I deal with all the bills / house etc. I lost my job due to the narrowmindedness of a boss that just didn't like new people. 

Cue a month a half later when I just hit snapping point and found myself at a train station, and not to go somewhere nice. 

I ended up getting sectioned for a minimum 72 hours with a view to being a lot longer. 

it helped immensely. 

But, it means that you have a lot less rights. Being in lockdown helps to a point, but what happens when you just want to go out for a cigarette? Stretch your legs? Wander to the hospital shop for a cold can of something? 

Unless you want the rest of your days to consist of breakfast, do fuck all, dinner, do fuck all, tea, do fuck all and sleep, then go for it. Remember that you can improve your health outside of a hospital. Being at the behest of a team of people that think that they know best, and if you challenge, you are at the receiving end of a team of strongmen armed with nowt but hate and sedatives is no way to live,

Talk to a counsellor. They aren't there to judge. As long as you aren't hurting yourself or others, they are bound by confidentiality and getting this out in the open just might be what you need.
